title: AV1 long UVLC values can bypass libheif coded-size limits
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: The AV1 scanner used a UVLC reader that rejected values after 20 leading zero bits even though the format allows 31 for the field, then ignored the failure. This let libaom allocate an oversized frame after the security check. The advisory reports up to about 3.5 GB peak memory on a crafted small AVIF.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-ESNQYZED. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: The AV1 UVLC reader now follows the specification and rejects incomplete sequence headers; fixed in libheif 1.23.7. The confirmed affected configuration uses libaom for AV1 decoding; dav1d and FFmpeg independently enforce limits. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: An untrusted AVIF using a long AV1 UVLC value can bypass coded-size limits and cause excessive memory allocation when libaom configuration is used.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.
